name: Guangzhou
title: Ship UTM Guangzhou | Thickness Gauging on the Pearl River
description: Thickness measurement in Guangzhou and Nansha: hull structure UTM on bulk carriers, container ships and car carriers, pre-docking and renewal survey work.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships in Guangzhou
intro: Guangzhou's port runs from Nansha, near the mouth of the Pearl River, up to the older river port areas at Huangpu. Container ships, grain and coal carriers, car carriers and tankers call there, and the repair and building yards of the Pearl River Delta are within reach. A grain discharge at Nansha, a few days waiting off the river mouth or a slot in a Delta yard can each be turned into a measurement window for hull, holds, tanks or piping, with the team travelling from India for the job.

highlights.h: Nansha calls scoped to the cargo
highlights.p: Container ships, grain carriers and car carriers at Nansha each release different spaces during cargo work. The gauging list is built around what that particular cargo operation frees up, and agreed with the chief officer before arrival.

highlights.h: Estuary anchorage for the long windows
highlights.p: Off the river mouth, ships lying in ballast for a berth or for orders have nothing to load or discharge, so holds and ballast tanks can be opened for buyers' surveys, on-hire records and pre-docking measurements.

highlights.h: Typhoon season built into the plan
highlights.p: From early summer into autumn, tropical storms can stop launch traffic and deck work. Jobs falling in that season carry spare days and an agreed order of priority so the important spaces are measured first.

port.h: Guangzhou: the Pearl River port from Nansha to Huangpu
p: The port of Guangzhou stretches a long way along the Pearl River. Its deep-water heart is now Nansha, at the southern tip of the city near the river mouth, with container terminals, grain and bulk berths and a large vehicle terminal. Further upriver, the Huangpu and Xinsha port areas handle bulk, liquid and container cargo for the industrial districts of Guangzhou and Dongguan, and smaller river and coastal ships carry cargo inland through the Delta's waterways. Draught limits on the river channels decide how far up a ship can go, so the deep-draught ships stay at Nansha and the river reaches belong to smaller tonnage.

The ships reflect the Delta's economy. Container ships serve export manufacturing; bulk carriers bring grain, coal and other raw materials; car carriers load and discharge vehicles at Nansha; and product and chemical tankers serve terminals along the river. Many of these ships are in Asian trades with short voyages and frequent port calls, which keeps their hulls, decks and cargo spaces working hard and their gauging windows short. Frequent ballasting and deballasting on those rotations also keeps ballast tank coatings under constant wet-and-dry cycling, a reliable driver of corrosion in the upper parts of the tanks. The longer windows come at anchorage in the Pearl River estuary, where ships wait for berths or orders, and in the yards when they dock.

Guangzhou builds ships as well as handling them. CSSC's Guangzhou Shipyard International, on Longxue Island at Nansha, builds tankers and a range of other commercial ships, and other yards in the city and the wider Delta carry out repair and conversion work. Guangzhou is a base for Chinese shipowning and ship-management groups as well, so survey and docking decisions for ships trading far beyond the Delta are often taken here. For those owners a ship calling at Nansha is a convenient chance to collect condition data before committing to a yard.

facilities.h: From Nansha to Huangpu: gauging locations in Guangzhou
p: Hull gauging at Nansha fits around cargo work. Container ships release deck plating, coamings, piping and whatever tanks the stay allows; bulk carriers at the grain and coal berths open their holds after discharge; car carriers make their vehicle decks available deck by deck during loading and discharge. Upriver at Huangpu and Xinsha, smaller bulk carriers, tankers and coastal ships are gauged at their berths in the same way. Anchorage work in the estuary covers pre-purchase, on-hire and pre-docking gauging on ships in ballast, with the team boarding by launch from the agent's chosen landing point.

Yard work is the other half. Ships docking in Guangzhou or elsewhere in the Delta for renewal or intermediate surveys need gauging timed to the yard's cleaning and staging, and readings delivered quickly enough for steel renewal decisions. We plan the measurement points before the docking and complete them space by space as the yard releases tanks and holds. River-port berths upstream also deserve a note: ships there are often smaller and older, and their ballast tanks and deck fittings can show heavier wastage than the deep-sea tonnage at Nansha.
list: Nansha container terminals — container ships serving the Delta's export trade; lashing bridge supports, coaming corners, deck plating and scrubber outlets, scheduled around the stowage plan.
Nansha grain and bulk berths — Panamax and Supramax bulk carriers after grain or coal discharge; holds, hoppers and hatch covers measured once the holds are swept.
Nansha vehicle terminal — export car carriers; vehicle deck plating, ramps and hoistable panels measured as the stevedores clear each level.
Huangpu and Xinsha port areas — hull, tank and piping gauging on smaller bulk carriers, tankers and coastal ships alongside upriver.
Pearl River estuary anchorages — ships waiting off the river mouth for berths or orders; gauging for buyers, for charter delivery or ahead of a Delta docking.
Pearl River Delta repair yards — docking periods for renewal and intermediate surveys, with survey gauging and checks on renewed steel before undocking.

context.h: Regulation and market context in the Pearl River Delta
p: Guangzhou's port state inspections follow the Tokyo MoU and are made by China's Maritime Safety Administration. Bulk carriers with hold and hatch cover wastage, tankers with thinned deck piping and container ships with corroded lashing structures are the kinds of findings a superintendent would rather deal with through planned gauging than at an inspection. The Delta's inland waterways and coastal waters are covered by China's domestic emission control rules, and where open-loop discharge is barred, scrubber-fitted ships entering the river have to change how they run their systems.

The Delta is one of China's main export manufacturing regions, and the shipping that serves it is dominated by intra-Asia container services, regional bulk trades and vehicle exports. Car carriers have become a much more visible part of Nansha's traffic as Chinese vehicle exports have grown, and their multi-deck structure brings a gauging scope quite unlike a bulk carrier's: large areas of thin deck plating, ramps and hoistable decks rather than heavy hold structure. Guangzhou's position next to Shenzhen and Hong Kong also means a ship's owner, manager, charterer and class surveyor are often close at hand, which makes joint planning of a survey or condition inspection straightforward.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Guangzhou
jobs.p: Ship inspection in Guangzhou follows the port's cargo mix and the Delta's yards. We agree scope and access with the superintendent before arrival, time the team's travel from India to the berth, anchorage or dock date, and deliver readings on the class TM formats so they can be used directly in the survey or in the yard specification. Where the owner has earlier TM reports, measurement locations are matched to them.
list: Vehicle deck and ramp gauging on a car carrier loading export vehicles at Nansha, sequenced deck by deck with the chief officer and the stevedores.
A Panamax that has just discharged grain at Nansha: holds and hatch covers measured while they are empty, in preparation for its intermediate survey.
Pre-docking gauging of a container ship's ballast tanks and deck structure at Nansha before it moves to a Pearl River Delta yard for its renewal survey.
Deck and cargo piping gauging on a product tanker alongside at an upriver terminal, concentrating on lines with a history of leaks.
Pre-purchase gauging of a bulk carrier at anchorage in the Pearl River estuary for a buyer whose technical team sits in Guangzhou.

logistics: Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport is the nearest gateway, followed by the road journey to Nansha or the upriver port areas; Hong Kong International Airport is an alternative, with onward cross-boundary travel that needs a mainland visa as well. The agent handles terminal passes and books launches for estuary anchorages, and summer and autumn typhoons can suspend those launch services at short notice. Mainland visas for technicians coming from India rest on an invitation letter, so the application goes in once the berth, anchorage window or dock date is confirmed.

faqs.q: Do container ships on short intra-Asia rotations have time for gauging at Nansha?
faqs.a: Some, if the scope is focused. A ship on a tight rotation will not open its ballast tanks at every call, but deck structure, hatch coamings, lashing bridges and machinery-space piping can be gauged during cargo work. Ballast tank gauging is better split across several calls or taken at anchorage, and we plan that split with the superintendent so the whole scope is covered before the survey.

faqs.q: Which Pearl River Delta yards can you work at?
faqs.a: We go to whichever yard the owner has booked; the team follows the ship. Access is arranged through the yard and the owner's site team, with the yard's own safety induction and permits. The measurement plan is prepared before arrival, so gauging can start as soon as the first tanks are cleaned and staged.

faqs.q: Do typhoons affect gauging work at Guangzhou?
faqs.a: They can. From early summer into autumn, typhoons and tropical storms can close anchorages to launch traffic and stop work on deck. Gauging at a berth or in a yard is less affected than anchorage work. When a job falls in the typhoon season, we build margin into the plan and agree with the superintendent which spaces take priority if the window shortens.

faqs.q: Can gauging for a sale be done while the ship waits in the estuary?
faqs.a: Yes. A bulk carrier or tanker in ballast at anchorage in the Pearl River estuary is a good subject for pre-purchase gauging: holds and ballast tanks can be opened, the ship is not working cargo, and the buyer's superintendent can attend. Readings are reported on a layout that lets the buyer compare them with the last class TM report.
